title: Secretary of State of Wyoming

context.text: The seat is open: Secretary of State Chuck Gray, a Freedom Caucus-aligned Republican, is running for the U.S. House rather than seeking re-election.
In the August 18 Republican primary, Short defeated Rachel Williams, chair of the Wyoming Freedom Caucus, and others in preliminary results; McCarty was unopposed in the Democratic primary.
Wyoming's Secretary of State oversees statewide elections and business registration, and is first in line for gubernatorial succession.

candidates.name: Robert Short
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18 Republican primary for the open seat.

priorities.text: Election administration conducted in a fair, honest and accurate manner, and partnering with county clerks on training, tools and resources; on the federal role he said: "I believe the federal government has no role in Wyoming elections. I would work with the federal government if the law directed me to do so."
Business regulation: stopping people who "take advantage of our privacy laws" to create sham corporations, and requiring that someone can be held responsible for a registered organization's actions.
Disclosure of donors to organizations that spend "dark money" in Wyoming.
Waiting to see the effects of recently enacted election-law changes before recommending more.
Keeping public lands in public hands: "I intend to use my office's seat on the board of land commissioners to keep public lands in public hands"
Getting "dark money" out of campaign financing and reducing the overlap between lobbying and campaign contributions.
Administering existing election law rather than advocating changes, which he says "would constitute a conflict of interest, or at least a breach of ethics."
Election security: "I would like to continue the work to rid drop in ballots, and streamline all clerks with the same up-to-date equipment to ensure secure ballots."
Open communication with county clerks and a minimal role for the federal government in elections.

researchNotes: Slate: Wyoming Secretary of State's 2026 General Election Candidate Roster (printed September 9, 2026) lists Short (R), McCarty (D) and Trujillo (Constitution). Positions are drawn from WyoFile's candidate questionnaire, published as submitted. None of the three took a documented side on proof of citizenship to register to vote, so no position or statement on that issue is recorded. Neither McCarty nor Trujillo has held office, and Short's county commission work is described only by his own materials.
